name: Closer
blurb: Real conversation that feels like winning.

cards.text: Tell them the specific thing they did this week that you keep replaying in your head. Specific or it doesn't count.
Finish this out loud, one each: 'I've been wanting to tell you…' No interruptions — the blank does the work.
cards.soften: Write it down, trade papers, read theirs silently.

cards.text: One true thing each, 60 seconds. The listener's only job is to listen — no fixing, no comebacks. Then trade.
cards.soften: 30 seconds each, same rule.

cards.text: If our relationship were a song right now, what's playing? Name it and defend it in one sentence.
What's something you miss that we used to do — not from lack of trying, just life? Name it. It goes back on the calendar this week.
Hold their hands and look at their eyes. Say the thing you've been carrying this week that's heavier than it should be.
cards.speak: They just hold your hands. That's the whole rule.
cards.soften: Sit back-to-back and say it without eye contact.

cards.text: Build a three-item menu each: one thing you want more of, one less of, one you're curious to try. Trade, then each picks one to 'order' this week.
cards.soften: Just name one item each.

cards.text: Make one wish about us out loud. The other answers either 'wish granted' (this week) or 'wish deferred' (name a date). No negotiating, no explaining.
Plan our next perfect Sunday out loud, minute by minute, starting at 9am. Both hands on the wheel.
cards.soften: Just agree on the breakfast.

cards.text: Do one tiny act of service for them right now, without asking what they want. They close their eyes while you decide.
cards.soften: Tell them what you WOULD do, and when.

cards.text: What's a question you wish I'd ask you more often? I'm asking it now. Answer it slow.
Each wave the magic wand: one thing you'd change about us. Wand-holders just say 'ok' — no defending. Wishes get re-read next month.
cards.soften: One wish each, deferred answers allowed.

cards.text: Slowly take off one item of their choosing.
cards.speak: While you do, tell them what you love about the person underneath, not just the skin.
cards.soften: Hold their hand against your heart for 30 seconds instead.

cards.text: Whisper the moment you knew you were done for. Be precise — the minute, the light, the sound in the room.
Kiss their neck for 30 slow seconds.
cards.speak: While you do, tell them the moment this week you were proudest of them.
cards.soften: Forehead kiss plus the compliment.

cards.text: Trade answers: what's a small thing the other did today that you noticed and appreciated silently? Silent appreciations get said now.
Tell them one thing they did this week that you keep replaying in your head.
What is a small everyday moment with them that still feels like a win when you think about it?
Share one way they made ordinary time feel better recently without even trying.
What is something you want more of from them that would make the weeks feel lighter?
Tell them about a quiet hope you have for the two of you over the next month.
What is one wish you have about us that you've been carrying but haven't said out loud yet?
Describe a recent moment when you felt especially glad to be on the same team.
Invite them to hear one specific appreciation you've been holding onto, then stay quiet while they take it in.
cards.speak: I've been meaning to tell you this because it stuck with me.
cards.soften: Share one short thing you appreciated about them this week.

cards.text: Offer a listen-first minute: ask them what would feel good to talk about right now, then only listen and reflect back what you heard.
cards.soften: Ask what is on their mind and give them space to answer fully.

cards.text: Make one clear wish about the two of you and invite them to answer with either 'wish granted this week' or 'wish deferred' plus a date.
cards.soften: Share one small hopeful wish and ask how it lands.

cards.text: Invite a soft trade: say 'I want more of ___ from you, and in exchange I'll give you ___' and mean both parts.
cards.speak: This is what would feel really good to receive, and here's what I want to offer back.
cards.soften: Share one thing you'd like more of and one thing you're happy to give.

cards.text: Replay a specific kind moment from this week out loud, adding why it still matters to you.
cards.soften: Mention one kind thing they did and why it landed well.

cards.text: Together, each build a three-item want-menu of small things that would make the coming week better. Trade menus and circle one item you can actually give.
cards.soften: Each name one small thing that would help, then choose one to try.

cards.text: Take turns granting or deferring one wish each. The grantor says 'wish granted this week' or 'wish deferred' and names a realistic date.
cards.soften: Each share one small wish and respond with a kind yes or later.

cards.text: Do a listen-first round: each person gets ninety seconds to speak about anything on their mind while the other only listens, then reflects one sentence back.
cards.soften: Each share for thirty seconds while the other simply listens.

cards.text: Trade framing challenge: each completes the sentence 'I want more of ___ from you, and in exchange I'll give you ___'. Both parts must feel genuine.
cards.soften: Each name one want and one offering in a lighter way.

cards.text: Together, name three specific things the other person did this month that still feel good to remember. Keep going until you both have a short list.
cards.soften: Each share one recent thing the other did that landed well.

cards.text: What is one small thing that always makes you feel a little more settled when you're around them?
Share a tiny detail from today that you are glad you got to experience with them, even if it was ordinary.
What is a simple way they could surprise you this week that would feel thoughtful rather than big?
Name one everyday ritual between you that you would miss if it disappeared.
Talk about the difference between a week that feels connected and a week that feels like you are just sharing a calendar.
Share what 'feeling chosen' looks like in ordinary days, not just special ones.
Discuss one small trade that would make both of you feel more supported in the next couple of weeks.
Thank them for something small they do that they would never expect to be thanked for.
Is there a light apology you feel you still owe them from anytime in the past year?
What is one question about us you've been quietly curious about but haven't asked yet?
What do you most need from the week ahead, in one clear sentence?
If money didn't matter, what dream job or daily work would you actually want?
What trait of theirs do you admire most when no one else is watching?
Share one real thing you have learned from being with them.
Is there a quiet fear about the future or about us that you've never quite put into words?
What song currently feels like it could be 'our song' even if you've never named it that?
What does calm actually look like for you on a regular day?
Invite them to receive sixty seconds of your full attention — phones down, eyes on them, no fixing, just presence.
cards.soften: Give them thirty seconds of undivided attention.

cards.text: Name one piece of invisible labor they handle that often goes unnoticed, and thank them for it out loud.
cards.speak: I see this thing you do, and it matters more than I've said.
cards.soften: Mention one helpful thing they regularly do and say thank you.

cards.text: Read them one short paragraph of a letter you would write if you were putting today's feelings on paper.
cards.speak: If I wrote this down for you, it would start like this…
cards.soften: Share one sentence you would put in a note to them.

cards.text: Ask them what they need most this week and then reflect back what you heard in your own words.
cards.soften: Ask what would help them this week and listen fully.

cards.text: Invite a two-minute 'finish this story together' improv: start a memory or imaginary scene and hand it back and forth.
cards.soften: Start a short shared memory and let them add one detail.

cards.text: Share one fear or worry you've kept light on purpose, and invite them to simply hold it with you for a moment.
cards.speak: I've been carrying this quietly and I want you to know.
cards.soften: Mention a small worry and let them respond however they want.

cards.text: Point out one trait you admire in them and give a specific recent example of it in action.
cards.soften: Name one quality you like and leave it at that.

cards.text: Sit in calm together for one minute — no topic, no fix, just shared quiet.
cards.soften: Share twenty seconds of comfortable silence.

cards.text: Together, each name one piece of invisible work the other carries. Acknowledge it without trying to solve anything.
cards.soften: Each mention one helpful thing the other does behind the scenes.

cards.text: Give each other sixty seconds of full attention in turn. The listener only nods, reflects, or says 'I hear you.'
cards.soften: Take thirty-second turns of focused listening.

cards.text: Build a short 'our song' shortlist together: each offers two candidates and you notice which ones both feel right.
cards.soften: Each suggest one song that feels like it belongs to both of you.

cards.text: Take turns finishing the same story: one person starts a real or imaginary scene, the other continues, then switch again.
cards.soften: Co-tell one short memory with each person adding a sentence.

cards.text: Each share what calm looks like for you, then find one overlapping detail you can protect for each other this week.
cards.soften: Each describe a calm moment and notice any common ground.

cards.text: Together, name one light question about the relationship that has felt slightly avoided, and decide whether today is a good day to open it.
cards.soften: Each mention one gentle curiosity and agree to park or explore it.

cards.text: What is one everyday thing that reliably helps you feel more settled?
If you could hand the other person a single helpful tool for the week, what would it be?
What is a small way they already make hard days a little easier?
Name one thing you are looking forward to in the next few days.
What kind of quiet feels good to you versus the kind that feels empty?
Talk about the difference between being busy together and actually feeling close.
Discuss what 'support' looks like on a Tuesday when nothing special is happening.
Share how you each like to be thanked so the appreciation actually lands.
Talk about a trait you hope you keep borrowing from each other over the years.
Discuss what a calm evening at home needs in order to feel restoring for both of you.
Share one thing you've learned about partnership simply by watching how the other person moves through the world.
What is one small ritual you would love to start together that you don't already have?
After tension cools, what helps you feel ready to come back toward each other?
What is the compliment from them you still remember most clearly?
What matters most to you in a partnership when everything else is stripped away?
How do you feel about phones at dinner or during focused time together?
What is one secret dream you've been carrying that you haven't fully shared yet?
After a hard moment, what helps you feel like we are good again?
What is one thing you want more of in the way the two of you handle conflict once the heat has passed?
Invite them to listen while you read one paragraph from any book out loud, chosen just for them.
cards.speak: I picked this because it made me think of you.
cards.soften: Share one short sentence from a book or note.

cards.text: Recreate a simple meal or snack that carries a memory for either of you.
cards.soften: Name the memory-meal and suggest making it soon.

cards.text: Say the redo: take one moment you wish you had handled more gently and say it again, the gentler way.
cards.speak: If I could say it again, it would sound like this.
cards.soften: Share one sentence you wish you'd said differently.

cards.text: Translate one 'I love you' into their preferred love language right now — through words, time, touch, service, or a small gift.
cards.soften: Do one small thing that matches how they like to receive care.

cards.text: Invite a sixty-second shared-goals check-in: name one thing you're both working toward this month.
cards.soften: Share one small goal you hope you're aligned on.

cards.text: Reveal one secret dream in a single clear sentence and let them simply hold it with you.
cards.speak: I've been carrying this quietly and I want you to know.
cards.soften: Share a lighter hope instead of a deep dream.

cards.text: Together, design one weekly ritual you could actually keep — when, where, and what makes it feel like yours.
cards.soften: Each suggest one small weekly idea and pick a favorite.

cards.text: Build a tiny gratitude jar moment: each write or speak three specific things from the past week and place them in a shared list.
cards.soften: Each name two things you appreciated this week.

cards.text: Do a love-language translation round: each person says 'I love you' in the way the other most easily receives it.
cards.soften: Each offer one gesture that matches the other's style.

cards.text: Take turns with the redo: each of you re-says one moment you wish had gone differently, and receives it kindly.
cards.soften: Each share one sentence of redo and receive it kindly.

cards.text: Hold a five-minute shared-goals check-in: name what you're building toward and one way you can support each other.
cards.soften: Each name one goal and one supporting action.

cards.text: What small daily ritual already makes the house feel more like home?
How do you know you're in a good headspace for a deeper conversation?
What is one value you hope never gets negotiated away between you?
Talk about inventing an anniversary that isn't on the calendar — a private date that only the two of you celebrate.
Discuss how each of you best learns the other's love dialect when it isn't obvious.
Share what a future-home negotiation would need to include so both of you feel heard.
